newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada preparing for big surpluses, brokerage says.
newsitem.headline: Canada preparing for big surpluses, brokerage says.

text.p: The Canadian government is billions of dollars ahead of budget targets and on track to run up huge surpluses during the next four years, a major Canadian brokerage said in a study released on Wednesday.
The report by CIBC Wood Gundy said the federal government should post a small budget surplus next year, which will grow exponentially over the balance of the next government's mandate.
Canada's Liberal government is running for re-election on June 2 largely on the basis of its fiscal performance during the last three and a half years.
The report suggested that the real fiscal choice facing Canadians during the election is how to direct surpluses to debt reduction, tax relief and program spending.

If program spending rises in line with inflation and population growth, current tax rates will lead to a C$60-billion annual surplus by the year 2000, said Jeff Rubin, chief economist with CIBC Wood Gundy.
There is no need to cut program spending to finance tax cuts when the federal government is so far ahead of its deficit reduction target, Rubin said.

At the same time, Rubin noted that the Liberal pledge to spend 50 percent of any budgetary surplus before offering tax relief would open the floodgates to an almost C$20 billion increase in program spending.

"With personal tax burdens already at record highs, do taxpayers really want to see their federal government spend half of a huge fiscal dividend, before they get to see any for themselves?" Rubin asked.
